page.intro: A route survey checks, before the first convoy, whether the longest and heaviest parts can pass every bend, junction and village on the way. This one does it for 84.3 m Vestas V172 blades from the Vestas blade plant in Goleniów to the five V172 commissioned in 2026 in the forest between Münster (Lech) and Thierhaupten — without any report or local knowledge of the route: the road, the difficult passages and every finding come from open data and the swept-path model alone.
page.method: No reports, two fixed points: from the blade yard in Goleniów to the first crane pad, the cheapest heavy-transport path on the road network — motorways, trunk and federal roads on the long haul, town streets (50 km/h or less) avoided eightfold, minor roads only within 30 km of either end. Fixed by hand are only the yard exit (Prosta → Granitowa → S3, the plant's heavy-load exit to the expressway) and, on the B 16 at Mittelstetten, the westbound exit over the B 16 bridge, where the shortest path would turn back into the eastbound exit ramp. Every 10 m is rated (wheels beyond the measured edge, blade overswing, leaving the right lane, tight turns, clear heights) and every difficult stretch becomes a passage on survey-grade official data (20 cm photo, 1 m laser terrain, surface model): one in Poland, seven in Brandenburg and fifteen in Bavaria (Mecklenburg-Vorpommern and Saxony-Anhalt serve the same data, but no passage lies there). The clear heights of more than 300 structures are measured against the 1 m laser terrain and, in Poland, Brandenburg and Bavaria, in the raw airborne laser point clouds (GUGiK, LGB and LDBV, flown 2021–2025): the road under each bridge and the top of its deck, with a typical deck depth assumed, because a scanner flying overhead rarely sees a deck's underside. Each passage was reviewed on the aerial photo.
page.overview: A route found and checked without any report or local knowledge: the cheapest heavy-transport path on the road network from the blade plant in Goleniów to the first crane pad, driven with a swept-path model of the transporter. The survey points are where the data say it gets difficult.

The Brandenburg laser point cloud (LGB) puts the top of the bridge deck 5.70 m above the A 11, so the low earlier estimate was no artefact: the convoy's 4.8 m is clear only if the deck is less than 0.90 m deep, a slim slab. factory.name: Vestas blade plant, Goleniów (LM Wind Power until September 2025)
facts: The V172 blades are built here: LM Wind Power built them for Vestas under contract; Vestas signed the takeover on 15 May 2025 and runs the plant since 5 September 2025, saying it will continue to deliver V172-7.2 MW blades.
Opened 2009, extended 2017, about 400 employees; 25 km north-east of Szczecin, beside the S3 expressway.
The convoy leaves the blade yard on Prosta and Granitowa and joins the S3 at the Goleniów junction — the first survey point.
